title: Pacific Wave, Museo Fortuny poster
lede: April Greiman’s poster for an exhibition of California graphic design in Venice: a stippled wave photograph, pink and black fields with irregular white holes, and tilted bitmap type.
summary: Pink, black, and yellow fields with white blob-shaped holes, a dotted gradient wave, and tilted bitmap “pacific wave” lettering. April Greiman, 1987.

source.label: V&A: Pacific Wave, Museo Fortuny, E.1499-2010

evidence.note: Inspected the V&A photograph of object E.1499-2010 (image 2011EN9649, 1200 × 1600) in a scratchpad copy. Not stored.

styles.note: Partial fit: the tilted type, gradient bars, and layered fields belong to the style, but the letters are rough bitmaps and type plays a small part.

context: The V&A holds the poster as E.1499-2010, colour offset lithograph, 98.5 × 68 cm, and describes it as a poster for “Pacific Wave”, an exhibition of California graphic design at the Museo Fortuny, Venice, September 1987. [V&A E.1499-2010](https://collections.vam.ac.uk/item/O1176678/).
observed: A yellow bar runs across the top and down the right side, fading through red to blue.
Large black and hot-pink fields fill the sheet. Irregular white shapes with soft, blob-like edges cut holes through them.
A photograph of a breaking wave is rendered in coarse white stipple over a yellow-red-blue gradient panel.
“pacific wave” runs on a rising diagonal in white bitmap letters with broken, ragged edges, followed by dotted lines. A second, smaller copy sits on the pink field.
Small text runs vertically in narrow black and pink strips at the left.
interpretation: This is the style at its most digital. The ragged bitmap letters come near the grunge counter-rule, but they are low-resolution output, not deliberate damage. Treat it as the edge of the style, not a model for it.
borrow: Run a gradient bar around two edges of a composition as a frame.
Set a title on a steep diagonal and repeat it smaller in another layer.

rights.statement: No image is stored. The photograph is © Victoria and Albert Museum, London. April Greiman is living, so the design is in copyright.
